records.name: Sachsen
records.current_summary: Sachsen is the epicentre of both legislative hostility and organised street violence against queer events in Germany. In 2024–2025, Pride events across the state were disrupted by coordinated far-right counter-mobilisations: a mob of more than 700 neo-Nazis assembled at the Bautzen parade (summer 2024, the season's largest organised counter-protest, alongside nine further pride-event incidents statewide); in Döbeln (September 2025), a simultaneous counter-march through town produced seven criminal offences and a formal investigation after a public Hitler salute; in Dresden (2025), neo-Nazis attempted to disrupt the parade with a counter-protest. The state also co-authored the Bundesrat initiative (with Sachsen-Anhalt and Thüringen) to tighten the federal Self-Determination Act (SBGG), an organised multi-state attempt to roll back trans self-ID rights.  Mitigating factors: police protection let all events proceed without physical harm to attendees; the Bautzen 2025 parade ran under heavy police presence; Leipzig and Dresden's inner neighbourhoods remain comparatively safe. The violence pattern is concentrated in small and mid-sized towns and rural areas rather than the major urban centres.  Deviation: −0.16 from the national score (0.71). The spread reflects the only state combining a multi-city pattern of organised street attacks with active legislative hostility toward trans rights. Below Brandenburg (0.64), whose violence is concentrated in one city (Cottbus) with a positive Staatsschutz response; below Sachsen-Anhalt (0.63) which shares the SBGG initiative but lacks documented street attacks. The urban/rural caveat applies: this score reflects the state-wide pattern, not Leipzig's everyday environment.

sources.claim: German news report (31 May 2025): CSD participants marched through Dresden while neo-Nazis staged a counter-protest attempting to disrupt the parade - the Dresden incident in the statewide pattern.

German regional radio (2025): after the 'Fall Liebich' case, the states of Sachsen, Sachsen-Anhalt and Thuringen demand tightening of the federal Self-Determination Act, alleging abuse of the self-ID right - a joint Bundesrat initiative to restrict how trans and intersex people use legal gender change; the legislative-hostility evidence for this state's co-authorship.

records.name: Bauchi
records.current_summary: Bauchi is the only Nigerian state with a carried-out Sharia death-by-stoning sentence for same-sex acts in the modern record: on 28 June 2022 a Sharia Court in Ningi LGA sentenced three men to death under Section 134 of the Bauchi State Sharia Penal Law (2001), following arrest by the Hisbah religious police on 14 June 2022 and conviction on their own admissions; the Hisbah head publicly announced the case. Lower-level practice includes secret floggings (March 2014, four men 15 lashes each, trial held in secret) and a Sharia Commission charging a dozen men with belonging to a 'gay club' (January 2014). LGBTQ+ groups warned the stoning could trigger similar cases across the Sharia block.  Mitigating institutional fact: the Upper Sharia Court of Bauchi State has repeatedly quashed stoning sentences on appeal (Babaji 2003, Chiyawa 2003), per Amnesty International. However, the 2022 conviction and announcement demonstrate active enforcement capacity. Score 0.064 below the national 0.08, reflecting the only actual capital-punishment-for-homosexuality event in Nigeria plus ongoing Hisbah arrests.  Well below Kano, which has equivalent statutory death-penalty text but no documented carried-out stoning, and far below the generic Sharia states, where enforcement documentation is thinner.

sources.claim: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (Reuters returns 401 to automated fetches); the underlying Reuters report (2 July 2022) covers the Ningi Sharia court sentencing three men - a 70-year-old among them - to death by stoning for homosexuality after a 14 June 2022 Hisbah arrest, the first time the death penalty has actually been imposed for homosexuality in Nigeria.

Amnesty International press release (2004): the Upper Sharia Court of Bauchi State quashed Jubrin Babaji's death-by-stoning 'sodomy' sentence (convicted 25 September 2003 under Section 133 of the Bauchi Sharia Penal Code Law 2001) for denial of counsel and a defective confession, following the quashing of Yunusa Rafin Chiyawa's conviction on 14 November 2003 - 'a number of cases where convictions and sentences to death have been quashed on appeal'. Also records a then-pending stoning appeal (Usman/Ibrahim) before a Sharia Court of Appeal in Niger State.

flags: 'the only Nigerian state with a carried-out Sharia death-by-stoning sentence for same-sex acts in the modern record' — sentencing is corroborated, 'only' and 'carried-out' are not (no execution reported; other states' sentences not excluded)

freshness.fact: Incident record (2014 floggings) unchallenged; corporal enforcement of sharia morality law in Bauchi continues to be cited in 2026 advisory context.

records.name: Kano
records.current_summary: Kano's Sharia Penal Code Law took effect 26 November 2000, prescribing 100 lashes plus up to one year's imprisonment for unmarried persons convicted of consensual same-sex activity, and stoning to death for married or previously married offenders. Kano hosts the most active Hisbah religious-police force in Nigeria, functioning as a parallel arrest authority beyond secular police. USCIRF's 2019 implementation study used 173 Sharia-court cases from 2017 in Kano, Sokoto, and Zamfara to document operational enforcement.  Score 0.054 below the national 0.08. The additional capital-penalty text, the most active Hisbah enforcement layer, and documented Sharia-court case volume justify this deviation. Above Bauchi, where the Sharia death penalty has actually been imposed, and above the generic Sharia states, where enforcement documentation is thinner.

records.name: Sokoto
records.current_summary: Sokoto's Sharia Penal Code Law took effect 31 January 2001 and prescribes stoning to death for married or previously married offenders convicted of consensual same-sex sexual activity (100 lashes where unmarried), with ta'azir discretionary punishment (up to 100 lashes and/or imprisonment) extending to same-sex acts between women and to cases involving a minor. This is the most capital-heavy statutory text within the twelve-state Sharia block. Hisbah religious-police activity is documented in Sokoto. USCIRF's 2019 case-level study covers Sokoto alongside Kano and Zamfara.  Score 0.054 below the national 0.08, driven by the explicit death-by-stoning text and documented Sharia-court caseload. Tied with Kano: Kano pairs death text with the most active Hisbah; Sokoto pairs the stoning text directly with USCIRF case evidence. Both are above Bauchi, where a stoning sentence was actually carried out.

records.name: Yobe
records.current_summary: Yobe is one of the twelve states operating a parallel Sharia criminal-code system - its Sharia penal code took effect 26 December 2000 - and one of five states (with Kano, Bauchi, Sokoto, Zamfara) where Hisbah religious-police activity is specifically documented by the USCIRF report. Sharia courts have criminal jurisdiction for Muslims, criminalising conduct beyond the federal statute including same-sex acts between women (ta'azir penalties). No trans-specific incident or carried-out capital sentence is on record for Yobe in this dossier.  Score 0.044 below the national 0.08. The combination of enacted Sharia criminal jurisdiction and documented Hisbah enforcement infrastructure justifies a deeper cut than the seven Sharia states without noted Hisbah presence. Yobe edges below Zamfara only because Hisbah is explicitly named; Zamfara's distinction is being the 2000 trigger for the whole cascade.

sources.claim: Human Rights Watch report section on the extension of Sharia to criminal law: Zamfara's governor triggered the cascade (Establishment Law 27 October 1999, in force 27 January 2000), and by 2002 twelve states - Bauchi, Borno, Gombe, Jigawa, Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Kebbi, Niger, Sokoto, Yobe, Zamfara - operate Sharia criminal jurisdiction. Sharia applies only to Muslims; non-Muslims are tried in parallel common-law courts, and the state attorney general oversees both systems.

UK Home Office Country Policy and Information Note on SOGIESC in Nigeria (Version 4.0, June 2025): the federal criminal code penalises same-sex male conduct (up to 14 years, attempted 3 years) and is silent on women; Sharia penal codes in the 12 northern states apply to Muslims, with death the maximum for men in all twelve and penalties for acts between women ranging from death (in a minority of states) to flogging and imprisonment; the enforcement-and-Hisbah section records public flogging of persons cross-dressing in 2023 and notes few secular cases reach court.

flags: one of five states (with Kano, Bauchi, Sokoto, Zamfara) where Hisbah activity is specifically documented by the USCIRF report
Sharia penal code took effect 26 December 2000

records.name: Zamfara
records.current_summary: Zamfara was the first Nigerian state to reintroduce Sharia criminal law - its Sharia Establishment Law was introduced on 27 October 1999 and came into force on 27 January 2000 - triggering a cascade of eleven more states by 2002. Hisbah religious-police activity is documented in Zamfara. USCIRF's 2019 implementation study covers Zamfara alongside Kano and Sokoto using 2017 case data, confirming operational Sharia-court function. No trans-specific incident or capital sentence is recorded for Zamfara in this dossier.  Score 0.034 below the national 0.08. The enacted Sharia framework plus Hisbah presence plus USCIRF case evidence justify the deviation. Above Yobe (0.04) by a marginal 0.01: Yobe and Zamfara share the same legal basis and Hisbah documentation; the difference is immaterial and both sit at the lower-Sharia tier. Well above Bauchi (0.02), Kano (0.03), and Sokoto (0.03) where capital-text or capital-sentence evidence is far stronger.

records.name: Borno
records.current_summary: Borno is one of the twelve northern states applying Sharia criminal law in parallel with the federal system since the 1999-2002 wave. The Sharia Penal Code criminalises same-sex acts between men and women for Muslims, with penalties reaching beyond the federal 14-year SSMPA term. No trans-specific incident, Hisbah activity, or USCIRF case documentation is on record for Borno in this dossier. The legal framework itself is the finding; absence of documented enforcement is a reporting-decay limitation (TIERs states its figures represent 'only a fraction of the true scale'), not evidence of safety.  Score 0.024 below the national 0.08. Same justification as the seven-state generic-Sharia bloc (Borno, Gombe, Jigawa, Kaduna, Katsina, Kebbi, Niger): enacted capital-capable criminal law adding a parallel court jurisdiction, but without the documented Hisbah enforcement layer or case-level evidence that pulls Yobe (0.04), Zamfara (0.05), Kano/Sokoto (0.03), or Bauchi (0.02) lower.

records.name: Jigawa

records.name: Katsina
records.current_summary: Katsina is inside the twelve-state Sharia criminal-law bloc that took shape between Zamfara's 2000 adoption and the full complement by 2002. Sharia courts have criminal jurisdiction over Muslims; the penal code criminalises same-sex acts including between women. No trans-specific incident or Hisbah activity documentation appears for Katsina in this dossier. The legal divergence from the secular SSMPA framework is the operative finding.  Score 0.024 below the national 0.08, matching the generic-Sharia tier. The deviation rests entirely on the enacted parallel system; absence of case-level evidence for Katsina (unlike USCIRF's Kano/Sokoto/Zamfara study) keeps it above those three. Below Borno (0.06, tied) with no additional differentiating signal.
